text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.14% today after oil prices climbed on geopolitical concerns—specifically, reports that the U.S. is preparing for potential strikes against Iran following the midterm elections. As a major refiner, MPC benefits when crude oil prices rise because it can sell refined products (gasoline, diesel, fuel oil) at higher margins relative to its input costs, especially when refineries are running at high capacity like the current 93.4%. The tick upward today reflects the market's recognition that oil supply risks are driving prices higher.

This reverses some of the sharp 6.6% drop MPC took on October 27th, when diplomatic signals suggested the Iran conflict might de-escalate. The stock remains down 9% over two weeks as investors weigh whether geopolitical oil-price support will hold against the reality that U.S. refinery utilization is already near peak levels and fuel inventories are elevated—factors that limit how much refiners can capitalize on crude strength.
